data.content_ref: inline:KIND: reduction. SRC_003's frozen cycle configurations reduce to the stable-matching obstructions of SRC_001/SRC_004: a 2-factor coloring with monochromatic cycles matched by a perfect matching of crossing edges is exactly the special case of a stable matching obstruction where every vertex has exactly one crossing edge (a perfect, not just maximal, matching). So SRC_003 depends on the matching-stability mechanism of SRC_001 but strengthens it by exhibiting an exp(Θ(n)) family of such obstructions, answering SRC_002's Poisson-count premise. The dispute among SRC_001/SRC_004 (consensus→0), SRC_002 (constant), and SRC_005 (consensus→1) turns on one quantity: the expected number of stable matching cuts reachable from a uniform random start. It is REFUTED IF the cycle-based configurations of SRC_003 are not themselves stable under the update rule (e.g., a vertex on a cycle with a crossing chord can flip), in which case the reduction collapses and the obstruction family is smaller than claimed.
